description: Compute the dew point from temperature and relative humidity with the Magnus formula (Alduchov–Eskridge constants b=17.625, c=243.04).

faqs.a: γ = ln(RH/100) + (b·T)/(c+T), then Td = c·γ/(b−γ), with b = 17.625 and c = 243.04 °C (Alduchov–Eskridge). T is in °C.
faqs.q: What is the Magnus dew-point formula?

faqs.a: The dew point is the temperature at which air becomes saturated and water condenses. A small gap between air temperature and dew point means humid, muggy air (and fog risk).
faqs.q: What does the dew point tell me?

faqs.a: A common rule: dew points above about 18°C (65°F) feel muggy; above 21°C (70°F) feel oppressive.

howto: Read the dew point plus a comfort reading.
